title: Florida House, District 48
what_it_does: Represents District 48 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Incumbent Republican Jon Albert defeated Jerry Carter in the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary. A closed party primary was held Aug. 18, 2026, which under Florida law means at least one other candidate (opposing-party, no-party or write-in) qualified for the Nov. 3 general election; that opponent's name could not be verified from search snippets.
verified_ballot_note: Brownstein/Rubin Turnbull's post-primary report and Ballotpedia record that Jon Albert (incumbent) defeated Jerry Carter in the HD 48 Republican primary (https://www.bhfs.com/insight/florida-2026-post-primary-election-report/; https://ballotpedia.org/Jon_Albert). The November opponent's name was not found. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.occupation: Business owner; U.S. Marine Corps veteran; former mayor of Frostproof
candidates.background: Jon Albert of Frostproof, born in Winter Haven in 1979, served nearly 10 years in the U.S. Marine Corps and holds a history and political studies degree from Chaminade University of Honolulu. He served on the Frostproof City Council from 2016 to 2024 and as mayor from 2020 to 2024 before winning the District 48 House seat in 2024. He lists his occupation as business owner.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary over Jerry Carter

record.item: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.

Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

Voted yes on CS/HB 1517 (2025), which would have allowed parents to sue for the wrongful death of an unborn child (excluding the mother and providers of lawful care); passed the House 79-32 on April 9, 2025 and died in the Senate.

Voted yes on CS/HB 289 (2026), which would have allowed parents to sue for the wrongful death of an unborn child (excluding the mother and providers of lawful care); passed the House 76-34 on Jan. 15, 2026 and died in the Senate.

Voted yes on final House passage of CS/HB 1205 (2025), the law (Ch. 2025-21) that added new rules, registration requirements and penalties for citizen initiative petition drives; passed 81-30 on May 1, 2025.

abortion.summary: Supports abortion access in cases of rape, incest, threats to the life or health of the mother, severe fetal abnormalities, and other circumstances a woman and her physician decide are medically best.
abortion.quote: I support access to abortion in cases of rape, incest, threats to the life or health of the mother, severe fetal abnormalities, and other circumstances where a woman, in consultation with her physician, determines it is the best medical decision.

healthcare.summary: Would protect Medicaid coverage, expand preventive care and strengthen community health centers; does not call for Medicaid expansion.

growth.summary: Says state and local governments should be partners and wants local decision-making restored on housing, transportation and development.
growth.quote: Florida's state and local governments should be partners, not competitors.
